**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

The e-business Hosting Agreement imposes no minimum purchase or volume commitment on Bluefly:

- **§ 4.1 (Charges)** ties all Charges to Services actually ordered under Order Forms and Service Option Attachments, specified as one-time, installment, recurring or usage — i.e. payment for usage or ordered Services only.
- No take-or-pay, shortfall, committed-spend or usage-cap language appears anywhere (searches for "minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume/usage limits all returned nothing).
- **§ 11.5 (Capacity Planning)** only allocates responsibility for determining and requesting capacity; it does not commit Customer to any capacity level.
- Exit protection is in place: **§ 3.4** gives Customer convenience termination on one month's notice at any calendar month end, and **§ 3.2** renewal is terminable by either party on 90 days' notice.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged: § 3.4(b) preserves early termination charges "if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments," and Attachment A is not in the reviewed text — worth confirming on diligence that no early termination charge operates as a de facto commitment. That contingent cross-reference is not itself a minimum commitment, so no redline is warranted.
